assets.name: Smoke measurement
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Current smoke density from the optical chamber — direct input of the alarm decision.

securityGoals.rationale: A smoke density value is not secret.

securityGoals.formalDescription: The smoke measurement shall be protected against manipulation between optical chamber and alarm decision.
The smoke measurement shall reach the alarm decision continuously; loss shall be detected and reported as a fault.
securityGoals.rationale: The alarm decision needs a continuous measurement; a lost stream must become a fault.
Single measurement values are not evidence; alarms are recorded in the audit log (DA-010).

assets.name: Calibration parameters
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Optical calibration coefficients, sensitivity factors, reference values. Manipulation shifts every measurement — silently.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Calibration parameters shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
securityGoals.rationale: Coefficients are product know-how, not a security secret.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Calibration parameters shall only be changed by an authorised calibration procedure and shall be integrity-protected at rest.
Calibration parameters shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: Loaded at start-up; a missing calibration leads to a fault state, not to a silent failure.

assets.name: Alarm configuration
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Alarm and pre-alarm thresholds, verification delay, zone/address assignment.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Alarm configuration shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
securityGoals.rationale: Thresholds are documented in the commissioning report.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Alarm thresholds, delays and zone assignment shall be integrity-protected at rest and in transit.
Alarm configuration shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
Only authorised maintenance personnel shall change the alarm configuration.
securityGoals.rationale: Only authorised maintenance personnel may change thresholds, delays and zones.

assets.name: Controller firmware
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fire not detected" (fatality); contributes [indirect] to "Alarm not transmitted" (fatality)

properties.description: Firmware image of the controller MCU: alarm logic, protocol stacks, authentication, WLAN.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Controller firmware shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
Only firmware signed by the manufacturer shall be installed and executed on the controller.
Controller firmware shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

assets.name: Sensor firmware
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Firmware image of the sensor MCU (measurement, diagnostics, sensor-bus protocol).

securityGoals.formalDescription: Sensor firmware shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
Only firmware signed by the manufacturer shall be installed on the sensor head.
Sensor firmware shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

properties.description: Maintenance password hash, Wi-Fi PSK, TLS server key.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Device credentials shall not be readable via debug ports, flash dumps or the maintenance interface.
Device credentials shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Device credentials shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

properties.description: Network settings, device name, update server URL.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Device and network configuration shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
Device and network configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Device and network configuration shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

assets.name: Alarm event
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Alarm not transmitted" (fatality)

properties.description: Alarm / pre-alarm message with zone and address — the output of the safety function.

securityGoals.rationale: An alarm is meant to be seen.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Alarm events shall reach the fire panel unaltered.
Alarm events shall reach the fire panel within the EN 54 response time.
securityGoals.rationale: The alarm must reach the panel within the EN 54 response time.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Actions on Alarm event shall be attributable and recorded tamper-evidently.

properties.description: Heartbeat, diagnostic status (LED ageing, contamination), fault signal to the panel (EN 54).

securityGoals.rationale: Status and fault signals are not secret.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Detector status and fault signal shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Detector status and fault signal shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: A missing heartbeat must be noticed by the panel.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Actions on Detector status and fault signal shall be attributable and recorded tamper-evidently.

properties.description: Alarms, logins, configuration changes, updates, boot results — evidence after a fire event (liability, insurance).

securityGoals.formalDescription: Audit log shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure.
securityGoals.rationale: Contains user names and configuration history.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Audit log shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Audit log shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
Alarms, logins, configuration changes and updates shall be recorded tamper-evidently.

assets.name: Panel commands
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Alarm not transmitted" (fatality)

properties.description: Reset, silence and test commands from the fire panel. Not authenticated on the loop.

securityGoals.rationale: Panel commands are not secret.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Panel commands shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Actions on Panel commands shall be attributable and recorded tamper-evidently.
Reset, silence and test commands shall only be accepted from the authentic fire panel.
securityGoals.rationale: A spoofed reset or silence cancels a real alarm.

assets.name: Smoke detection
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Detect smoke reliably and in time (EN 54-7 response threshold).

securityGoals.formalDescription: Smoke detection shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
securityGoals.rationale: Detection must not be suppressed or falsified.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Smoke detection shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: Detection must be available permanently (EN 54-7).

assets.name: Alarm signalling
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [direct] to "Alarm not transmitted" (fatality)

properties.description: Signal an alarm to the fire panel — via the loop protocol and the hard-wired alarm contact.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Alarm signalling shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
securityGoals.rationale: The alarm signal must not be altered on its way to the panel.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Alarm signalling shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: Alarm signalling must be available permanently (EN 54-2 interface).

assets.name: Fault monitoring
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Detect and report detector faults (sensor-bus loss, contamination, LED failure) so an out-of-service detector does not go unnoticed.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Fault monitoring shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
securityGoals.rationale: A detector must not report OK while it is out of service.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Fault monitoring shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: Faults must be reported within the EN 54 fault-signal time.

properties.description: Download, verify and install controller and sensor firmware.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Firmware update shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Actions on Firmware update shall be attributable and recorded tamper-evidently.
Only authorised roles shall be able to change Firmware update.

properties.description: Technician login, threshold and network configuration, password change.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Maintenance and configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Actions on Maintenance and configuration shall be attributable and recorded tamper-evidently.
Only authorised roles shall be able to change Maintenance and configuration.

properties.description: Trust anchor of the update chain — a compromise reaches every device in the field.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Firmware update server shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
securityGoals.rationale: The update server is the trust anchor for every device in the field.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Firmware update server shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.
securityGoals.rationale: Updates are not time-critical; the detector keeps working without the server.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Firmware update server shall only be accepted from authenticated sources.
securityGoals.rationale: Devices must only accept updates from the authentic server.

assets.name: Controller unit
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Alarm not transmitted" (fatality)

properties.description: Controller MCU with alarm evaluation, panel interface, WLAN.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Controller unit shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Controller unit shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

assets.name: Optical sensor head
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fire not detected" (fatality)

properties.description: Sensor MCU with optical chamber, calibration and diagnostics.

securityGoals.formalDescription: Optical sensor head shall be protected against unauthorised modification; manipulation shall be detected.
Optical sensor head shall be available when required; a loss shall be detected and reported.

properties.description: People in the protected area; primary protection target of the detector (EN 54).
Emergency responders who rely on the reported zone/address.
Premises and goods protected by the fire detection system.

relations.rationale: The update process installs the sensor image.

properties.notes: Measurement and diagnostic status, ~10 Hz. Loss of the stream is detected by P-5 (sensor-bus timeout → fault).

properties.safetyRationale: Alarm message to the fire panel is the safety function output (EN 54).

properties.notes: The panel polls every loop address cyclically; a missing answer is shown as a fault on the panel.

properties.safetyRationale: Hard-wired alarm path, independent of the bus protocol.

properties.notes: Secure boot: image and signature are read before execution.
Post-flash readback verification.
Halt CPU, read/write RAM and flash (calibration, firmware).

Reset, silence, test. Not authenticated on the loop protocol.
Remote optical sensor head (smoke chamber, LED/photodiode, sensor MCU). Connected to the controller enclosure by a field-wired RS-485 sensor bus.
Secure boot verifies the controller image (P-8). Debug port still enabled — see JTAG interface.

Alarm decision: smoke density vs. threshold, verification delay, zone assignment. Drives the alarm relay and the fire-panel message.
properties.securityControls: Watchdog, plausibility check of measurements, alarm on sensor-bus loss (fail-safe)

properties.notes: Downloads the update package via the Communication Handler, verifies signature and rollback counter, writes the controller image to flash and forwards the sensor image to the sensor head.
properties.securityControls: Firmware signature check, rollback counter, A/B image fallback

properties.notes: WLAN driver (IEEE 802.11 b/g/n): station mode towards the site access point. Uses the Wi-Fi PSK from the device configuration flash. Does not terminate TLS.
Fire-panel protocol stack (RS-485 loop): alarm and status messages to the panel, reset/silence/test commands from the panel. Replaceable by a 868 MHz radio module.
Checks the maintenance login and authorises configuration changes. Gap: a single shared maintenance password, no roles — every authenticated user may change thresholds and credentials.
Root of trust: verifies the controller image before execution and reports the boot result.
Persists security-relevant events (alarms, logins, updates, boot results, WLAN events) — evidence after a fire event (EN 54, CRA).
Alarm thresholds, pre-alarm level, verification delay, zone/address assignment.
properties.safetyRationale: Manipulated threshold or delay = no alarm, delayed alarm or false alarm

properties.notes: Maintenance password hash, Wi-Fi PSK, TLS key, network settings.
WPA2/WPA3-Personal. Always on — also outside maintenance windows. No protection against de-authentication or jamming.
Potential-free alarm contact, wired to the conventional zone input of the fire panel.
Gap: enabled in production. Target state: permanently disabled (fused off).
Gap: enabled in production. Target state: permanently disabled (fused off).
EN 54-2 control and indicating equipment, operated by the building owner.

threatProfile.rationale: Access to the detection loop requires physical access to the building wiring

properties.notes: Service partner with laptop/app; configures thresholds and network settings.

threatProfile.rationale: Maintenance web UI only reachable from the site WLAN (proximity required)

properties.notes: Manufacturer backend; serves signed update packages over HTTPS.

threatProfile.rationale: Very high effort, but every device in the field is affected

properties.notes: Detector base / controller unit: alarm evaluation, fire-panel interface, alarm relay, WLAN for maintenance and firmware updates.
Gap: debug port not locked in production, no readout protection — calibration and firmware readable/writable after opening the enclosure.
Monitors LED ageing, chamber contamination, temperature/humidity. Reports faults (EN 54 fault signal) to the controller.
Receives the sensor firmware image from the controller via the sensor bus, writes it to the sensor flash and reads it back for verification.
properties.securityControls: Firmware signature check before flashing, post-flash readback

properties.notes: Optical calibration coefficients, sensitivity factors, factory reference values.
properties.safetyRationale: Manipulated calibration = systematically wrong measurement, undetected until the next calibration check

properties.notes: LED pulse control, ADC sampling of forward/side scatter, smoke density calculation. Reads calibration parameters at start-up and after recalibration.
Screw terminals of the field-wired sensor bus between sensor head and controller.
JTAG/SWD adapter of an attacker with physical access (or a service tool left connected).

threatProfile.rationale: Requires opening the enclosure (tool) and a JTAG adapter

properties.complianceRelevance: CRA Annex I §1(3) — EN 54-7 / EN 54-2 interface (alarm decision and transmission)

threatProfile.rationale: Operated by the building owner; shared PSK, rogue AP possible within radio range

properties.notes: HTTPS endpoint of the controller: maintenance web UI (server) and update download (client). Hands logins to P-7 Maintenance Authentication Service and downloads to P-12 Firmware Update Manager.
properties.securityControls: TLS 1.2+: server certificate for the maintenance web UI, server-certificate validation towards the update server

properties.notes: Detection loop to the fire alarm control panel.
Controller-side terminals of the sensor bus.
Ring buffer with hash chain (tamper-evident). Oldest entries are overwritten.

hazards.description: Smoke is present but the detector does not reach the alarm state (blinded or manipulated measurement, raised threshold, wrong calibration, compromised firmware, out-of-service detector not noticed).
hazards.label: Fire not detected
hazards.rationale: Fire and toxic smoke spread without evacuation — EN 54-7 detection function lost.

hazards.description: The detector decides on alarm but the fire panel does not receive it (loop message suppressed or spoofed reset/silence, relay path manipulated, panel interface compromised).
hazards.label: Alarm not transmitted
hazards.rationale: Panel does not trigger sounders, fire brigade call or extinguishing — same consequence as a missed detection.

hazards.description: The alarm is raised too late (verification delay or pre-alarm stage extended, alarm held back by the firmware).
hazards.label: Delayed alarm
hazards.rationale: Available safe egress time shrinks; harm grows with the delay.

hazards.description: Alarm without fire (threshold lowered, calibration shifted, spoofed test command, manipulated firmware) — unwarranted evacuation, possible release of an automatic extinguishing system, loss of trust in alarms.
hazards.label: False alarm
hazards.rationale: Panic and falls during evacuation; repeated false alarms lead to alarms being ignored or detectors being switched off.

hazards.description: The alarm reaches the panel with a wrong zone/address (manipulated zone assignment, altered alarm message).
hazards.label: Wrong fire location reported
hazards.rationale: Responders search the wrong area; rescue and firefighting are delayed.

info.description:
Industrial fire detector based on optical light-scattering measurement. A remote sensor head (optical chamber, sensor MCU) detects smoke particles through forward and side scattering of an LED light beam and streams the measurement over a field-wired RS-485 sensor bus to the controller unit. The controller evaluates the alarm condition, signals alarms and faults to the fire alarm control panel (RS-485 detection loop plus a hard-wired alarm contact) and logs security-relevant events. Configuration and firmware updates are performed via WLAN (maintenance web UI, update server).

Safety-critical characteristic: availability and integrity of the detection and alarm-signalling functions are safety-critical — a missing, delayed or mislocated alarm in the presence of smoke can endanger human lives (EN 54-7, EN 54-2).
info.name: Smoke Detector

warnings: 3 risk(s) based on uncertain threats — confirm relevance in Threat Eval

threats.attackDescription: Attacker impersonates an authorized person (e.g. maintenance technician) to gain physical access to the boundary interior
threats.causeDescription: Physical access control relies on single-factor authentication — no second factor prevents impersonation
threats.evalNote: The device does not control physical access; building access control is the operator's responsibility.
threats.threatDescription: Physical boundary identity spoofing — attacker impersonates authorized personnel to gain physical access

threats.attackDescription: Attacker opens the enclosure without triggering any alarm, gaining access to internal components
threats.causeDescription: No tamper detection mechanism — unauthorized opening is undetected
threats.evalNote: Enclosure opened without trace (no tamper switch, no seal) — gateway to JTAG and to blinding/covering the optical chamber.
threats.threatDescription: Physical boundary tampering — unauthorized physical access to boundary interior

threats.attackDescription: Attacker accesses boundary and performs actions without any record being created
threats.causeDescription: No physical monitoring or access logging at boundary — who accessed it and when is unknown
threats.evalNote: Opening the enclosure leaves no record — manipulations (e.g. covered chamber) cannot be attributed or even noticed.
threats.threatDescription: Physical access without audit trail — actions at physical boundary cannot be attributed

threats.attackDescription: Attacker measures power consumption or EM emissions and extracts cryptographic keys
threats.causeDescription: Physical boundary provides no electromagnetic shielding — internal operations are observable
threats.evalNote: Side channels add nothing while JTAG is unlocked (direct readout is easier). Re-evaluate after JTAG lock (M-CB-E-001).
threats.threatDescription: Side-channel observation — sensitive data extracted via physical measurements

threats.attackDescription: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability
threats.causeDescription: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed
threats.evalNote: Device destroyed or unpowered — detector out of service.
threats.threatDescription: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack

threats.attackDescription: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication
threats.causeDescription: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed
threats.evalNote: Privilege gain after opening the enclosure is the JTAG path — assessed on the JTAG interfaces.
threats.threatDescription: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts communication; without a defined fail-safe state, outputs may drive actuators dangerously
threats.causeDescription: No deterministic fail-safe output state defined — actuator outputs are unpredictable under fault
threats.evalNote: Output state on communication loss not defined for a safety-relevant communication task (sensor bus / panel loop). Outages must lead to a defined fault state.
threats.threatDescription: Undefined fail-safe output state — process outputs reach arbitrary values on communication loss

threats.attackDescription: Attacker observes process output and extracts sensitive configuration data, credentials, or business information
threats.causeDescription: Process outputs or error messages contain sensitive information — no output filtering applied
threats.evalNote: Task processes no confidential data (P-8 holds only the public verification key).
threats.threatDescription: Process data leakage — sensitive data processed by the process is exposed

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts communication to the safety system causing it to fail safe or fail dangerous
threats.causeDescription: Safety-critical communication has no redundant path and lacks DoS protection
threats.evalNote: Safety-relevant communication task (sensor bus / panel loop) disrupted by bus flooding — detected as fault, but alarm transmission is blocked while it lasts.
threats.threatDescription: Safety system denial of service — attacker disrupts safety-critical communication

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disables Secure Boot to execute malicious firmware that persists across device resets
threats.causeDescription: Secure Boot is not enforced or can be bypassed via debug interface
threats.evalNote: All tasks of one MCU share one firmware image and one boot check — assessed once per MCU (P-8 controller, P-4 sensor).
threats.threatDescription: Secure boot bypass on embedded system — attacker bypasses firmware signature verification

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts communication; without a defined fail-safe state, outputs may drive actuators dangerously
threats.causeDescription: No deterministic fail-safe output state defined — actuator outputs are unpredictable under fault
threats.evalNote: Behaviour of the optical measurement / diagnostics on internal failure not defined — a silent wrong output must become a fault.
threats.threatDescription: Undefined fail-safe output state — process outputs reach arbitrary values on communication loss

threats.attackDescription: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles
threats.causeDescription: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests
threats.evalNote: No externally reachable input that could exhaust this task; covered by the bus/interface DoS threats.
threats.threatDescription: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service

threats.attackDescription: Attacker replaces embedded process firmware to disable security checks or introduce a backdoor
threats.causeDescription: No cryptographic code signing on embedded process firmware
threats.evalNote: Sensor update handler firmware modified — sensor MCU has no secure boot.
threats.threatDescription: Embedded process firmware tampering — attacker modifies firmware of embedded process component

threats.attackDescription: Process or its operator denies having executed a command that affected the system
threats.causeDescription: Audit log is absent, incomplete, or not tamper-proof
threats.evalNote: Sensor-update and boot results are reported to and logged by the controller (P-12 / P-10).
threats.threatDescription: Process action repudiation — process denies having performed an action

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disables Secure Boot to execute malicious firmware that persists across device resets
